title: OIP v0.6.1 operation operands
summary: Positional operand layout of every OIP v0.6.1 operation. The Core family and the operation opcode select exactly one layout of ordered words, ordered blobs and a deadline mode. Field names document the layout and never appear on the wire.
layout_rules: The family and the opcode select exactly one layout. A decoder MUST reject an opcode outside 1 through the operation count of its family with INVALID_FORMAT.
Words are read in table order and a layout MUST consume every word. A missing word or a trailing word is INVALID_FORMAT.
An optional field starts with a presence word that MUST be 0 or 1. Its fields follow only when the presence word is 1.
A counted set starts with a count word followed by that many items in strictly ascending order, so it has no duplicates.
A counted pair list starts with a count word followed by that many pairs whose first members are strictly ascending.
A tagged field is the last field of its layout. Its tag word selects one case, and that case fixes the exact number of remaining words.
Blobs are matched by position and the blob count MUST equal the layout's blob count.
An enumerated word MUST hold an accepted code. A word whose accepted codes are any takes every value; the enum only names the known codes.

A decoder runs with a nesting limit, the number of Core levels it may decode counting the outer Core. A canonical_core blob is decoded with that limit reduced by one, and a decoder MUST reject a Core it reaches with a limit of zero with INVALID_FORMAT.
A layout fault is INVALID_FORMAT. A failed check returns the error listed with that check. A nested canonical Core returns the error of its own decode.
A v0.6 decoder MUST reject an Operation field that operation_record does not list with INVALID_FORMAT.

operation_record.order: Fields appear in ascending tag order: the opcode, then every word, then every blob, then at most one appeal deadline alternative.

fields.name: words
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Ordered 64-bit operand words, one unpacked field per word.

fields.name: appeal_deadline_indefinite
fields.label: oneof appeal_deadline
fields.description: Indefinite appeal deadline. The only valid value is 1 (true).

fields.name: appeal_deadline_utc_seconds
fields.label: oneof appeal_deadline
fields.description: Finite appeal deadline in UTC seconds.

deadline_modes.absent: Neither appeal deadline field is present. A present deadline is INVALID_FORMAT.
deadline_modes.appeal: Absent, indefinite or finite. The finite form is the appeal deadline in UTC seconds. In this version the product treats absent and indefinite alike as no appeal deadline.

u64.description: Unsigned 64-bit integer. The field description gives its meaning.

call_sequence.description: Caller sequence number. With the Core principal as namespace it forms the caller-qualified call identifier.

revision.description: Ledger revision. With the Core authority_epoch it forms a commit cut.

commit_position.description: Ledger commit position of a retained result.

event_id.description: Event number within its origin domain. With that domain it forms an origin key.

asset_version.description: Asset version in a signed version vector.

record_reference.description: Reference to a terminal evidence record.

clock_interval.description: Interval on the ledger clock. A time-enabled profile counts the ledger clock in Unix seconds.

utc_seconds.description: UTC time in seconds since the Unix epoch.

code.description: Code of the enum named by the field.

amount_u256.description: Unsigned 256-bit integer as exactly 32 big-endian bytes. The product range is u64, so the first 24 bytes MUST be zero.

octets.description: A byte string whose length may be zero. The operand defines its allowed lengths.

proof.description: Non-empty authorization or evidence bytes. The configured adapter verifies them against the exact canonical fields.

canonical_core.description: Complete canonical encoding of a v0.6 Core, decoded with the nesting limit reduced by one. It is data and is not admitted again as a delivery.

endpoint_contexts_json.description: Compact JSON array of endpoint context objects with the keys endpoint, epoch, grants, dependencies and write_permissions in that order. The array is non-empty and its endpoint values are strictly ascending. The bytes MUST equal the reference serializer's re-encoding of the decoded value.

session_bindings_json.description: Compact JSON array of [session, {"principal": principal, "authority_epoch": epoch}] pairs with strictly ascending session values. The bytes MUST equal the reference serializer's re-encoding of the decoded value.

family.description: Core family (tag 12). The Core body field of a family has tag 15 plus the family code.

primary.description: Core primary code (tag 13). The decoder accepts 1 through 5. The codes have no names and no effect in this version.

secondary.description: Optional Core secondary code (tag 14). Any value is accepted and preserved with its presence. The codes have no names and authorize no product effect.

signature_scheme.description: Core signature scheme (tag 15). The reference profile uses SINGLE with Ed25519.

priority.description: Core priority (tag 24). CRITICAL requires ALL_OR_NOTHING and current privileged authority. The reference configuration does not grant that authority.

spend_kind.description: Kind of a spend. An ordinary spend accepts only ORDINARY and an enforcement spend accepts only the other kinds.

query_tag.description: Case of a typed query operand.

sync_mode.description: Mode of a state commitment synchronization call.

values.name: INITIAL
values.description: Install the first source snapshot for the stream.

values.name: INCREMENTAL
values.description: Advance the stream from its retained commitment.

values.name: FULL_RESYNC
values.description: Replace the retained entry with a source snapshot under a scoped FullResync grant.

response_kind.description: Kind of a correlated response. A recorded response reports a retained product outcome; a delivery response reports the delivery state; a refusal reports a validation refusal.

response_code.description: Code of a correlated response. Each code fixes its response kind and whether the commit position is present.

values.name: ORIGINAL_REJECTED
values.description: Exact original Debit closed without effect.

values.name: STATE_COMMITMENT_SYNCED
values.description: Commits the authorized stream entry. An exact authorized retry returns the same recorded result. Closest v0.5 outcome is ACK type PROCESSED.

values.name: STATE_COMMITMENT_MISMATCH
values.description: The mode or predecessor fails its check and consumes the call identifier. Use a fresh signed call after obtaining the current entry. Closest v0.5 outcome is STATE_HASH_MISMATCH.

values.name: STATE_COMMITMENT_STALE
values.description: The source position or origin event fails its freshness check and consumes the call identifier. Use fresh source evidence and a fresh signed call. There is no v0.5 equivalent.

values.name: SOURCE_ATTESTATION_REJECTED
values.description: The selected source registry or proof fails validation and consumes the call identifier. Correct the evidence and use a fresh signed call. Closest v0.5 outcome is INVALID_DRIVER_ATTESTATION.

call_prefix.description: Prefix of every ordinary, legal and spend call. The call identifier is the Core principal with call_sequence. The signed cut is the Core authority_epoch with revision. The binding is the origin, asset, owner, destination and recipient with the amount in the first blob.

fields.name: message_reference
fields.description: Caller message reference carried into the product payload.

fields.name: origin_epoch
fields.description: Authority epoch of the original request.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Funding owner at the origin domain.

credential.description: Optional lock credential of an ordinary command.

version_vector.description: Signed asset version vector of an ordinary command. An asset without an entry has version zero.

query.description: Typed query operand. The tag selects the queried value and its exact operands.

reference_profile.description: The Ed25519 reference configuration accepts only the operations whose reference_accepts value is true. It refuses every other operation with UNSUPPORTED_VERSION before admission, because that operation is outside the selected version profile, which is the version together with its accepted operation set.

responses.call_identifier: A call carries a caller-qualified call identifier: the Core principal with the call_sequence word. Only calls have a correlated response.
responses.delivery_and_refusal: Every delivery and refusal code applies to every call. The recorded codes of each call are listed with the operation.

blobs.name: original_core
blobs.description: Canonical Core of the original call in its original bytes.

checks.rule: The nesting limit is at least 2, which leaves one level for original_core.
A commit is present only when kind is RECORDED.
The original has the version and deployment of this Core, its principal equals caller_namespace, and its source and target domains are this Core's target and source domains.
The original is not a correlated response.
A CurrentCommitment query has no correlated response.
An original call has the call identifier (caller_namespace, call_sequence). When it is a Debit, a present commit position equals its revision.
An original exact receipt query carries a call with the deployment, source domain, target domain, principal and authority epoch of that query and version 6.
An original exact receipt query carries a call with the call identifier (caller_namespace, call_sequence). When that call is a Debit, a present commit position equals its revision.
Codes 29, 39, 40 and 41 are recorded results of SyncCommitment. Code 29 carries a commit position and codes 39, 40 and 41 omit it.
When the original call is SyncCommitment, a known code has its declared kind and commit presence and is compatible with that call.
original_core equals the caller's retained canonical request and the call identifier equals that request's call identifier.
